redFirst.basis: regression task, expectRedFirst false. Mutation proven in a scratch copy of the tests dir (not the tree): dropping stdin=DEVNULL from _harness.git left 1/3 cases passing (2 FAIL, stdin case hangs to timeout); replacing the trace tail in the timeout message with a constant left the region_enter case FAIL. Restore asserted by diff against the tree copy (RESTORED). Note stdin=DEVNULL was already present at HEAD, so the stdin case locks it rather than fixing it.

outcome.technical: _harness.git now sets GIT_TRACE2_PERF to a per-call mkstemp scratch file (in the temp dir, which is the sweep's scratch TMPDIR), appends the last 2000 bytes (or a sentence saying empty/unreadable) as 'trace2 tail:' to the timeout RuntimeError, and always removes the file in finally. Added _trace_tail, TRACE_TAIL_BYTES, import contextlib. Cost measured: git status 100-call microbench ~7.0ms old vs ~8.3ms new (+~1.3ms/call); al-block runs ~42s and fixture git calls are a few dozen at most, so overhead is milliseconds, immaterial. Chose always-trace, not retry-on-timeout: a retry would re-run a possibly non-idempotent call and cost 60s more per hang, and a first hang would carry no trace. Added block gt-block / _git_stdin_cases (3 cases) to STAGES: hash-object --stdin in a child with an open unwritten stdin pipe returns the empty blob; status stalled in core.fsmonitor with timeout=3 reports a trace2 tail with a region_enter fsm_hook line; no git-trace2-* files left in temp dir. Full sweep exit 0 (335/335 files ok, 16466 cases); cp1252 pass exit 0 (335/335).
outcome.descriptive: A hung fixture git call now names the git region it stopped in, and the stdin-closed behaviour is locked by a case.
